Situations / Maw Pearl Crisis

Maw Pearl Crisis

Situation

The Pearl of Souls is intact inside the Red Lady wreck at the Shelfworks eastern edge, below Umberlee‘s domain boundary. It broadcasts a soul-collection signal across the planar fissure, drawing entities from the Elemental Plane of Water into the mortal sea. Removing it does not close the fissure, but it removes the attractor.

Current State

The fissure is geological and widening slowly. Under normal conditions it would leak elemental water and occasional passive drift. The Pearl changed the behaviour: the Leviathan followed the signal, a Ridgeback followed the signal, and the next incursion will do the same unless the Pearl is moved or silenced.

Auralis has shifted from passive watch to active containment. His old wards are failing under the Pearl’s beacon and the elemental surge. Umberlee cannot retrieve the Pearl because the wreck sits below her jurisdiction, so she is keeping Delmar Fisk alive and pressured as her proxy.

Delmar’s Secret

Delmar Fisk stole the Pearl from Umberlee‘s Blue Shrine at Vel Orn before the campaign began. When the fleet sank, Umberlee pressed five captains’ souls into him — the five who stayed loyal. The five he could have saved.

The secret Delmar carries: The crime that triggered the sinking was his. He made the call. He didn’t intend the outcome, but five people paid with their souls and he knows it.

What Delmar wants: Resurrect the five captains. If resurrection is impossible, release them so they can find their afterlives. Full resurrection is where his guardrails come off.

If the party learns the secret: The question is not whether they forgive him — the question is whether the five captains do.

DM Note

Players do not know the full shape of this. Delmar knows he carries voices. The party does not know about the five captains or what Delmar did.

Link of RelevanceDelmar stole the Pearl and carries the captains; Perrin is bound to Auralis; the party’s Maw choices decide whether the region stays navigable.

Narrative Devices

  • Loaded Gun: The Fleet Intelligence Room aboard the Red Lady may reveal who arranged the Pearl theft and why the wreck ended up beyond Umberlee’s reach.
  • Foreshadowing: Warm water, dead-fish smell, colour-shifted light below 80 ft, missing Sentinels, and salvage crews abandoning lower tiers.
  • Clock: Each world tick can bring another entity through or push the Leviathan higher into salvage zones.
  • Reversal Potential: Returning the Pearl to Umberlee may solve the attractor while empowering a hostile goddess; keeping it may save leverage while sustaining the crisis.

Key Facts

  • The Pearl is the active attractor; the fissure is the underlying geology.
  • The Leviathan and Ridgeback are confirmed directed incursions, not random sea monsters.
  • The Red Lady wreck and Pearl sit below Umberlee’s domain boundary.
  • Auralis predates Umberlee’s claim and guards the deeper machine around the fissure.
  • Salvagers are dismantling upper exhaust/pressure architecture — not harmless ruins.
  • Recovering the Pearl is the most consequential Season 1 action currently available.

Involved Parties

  • Delmar Fisk — stole the Pearl unknowingly as far as the party knows; five captains pressed into him; Umberlee’s necessary proxy.
  • Perrin Black-Jaw — saved by Auralis after the Vestra sank; bound as warlock; Leviathan is his quarry.
  • Umberlee — wants her artifact back; cannot access the boundary zone; uses Branca and the Dead Lady as pressure.
  • Auralis — last Antheri guardian; containing the fissure from below; responds more than he initiates.
  • Branca — senior Waveservant; civil scheduler and pressure valve for Umberlee.
  • Leviathan — first confirmed incursion; hunting near the wreck.
  • High Eyrie — has anomaly records and missing Sentinels but lacks the Pearl explanation.

Locations

  • Drowned Maw — fissure region and domain-boundary problem.
  • Shelfworks — visible newest layer of Antheri pressure/exhaust architecture.
  • Antheri Ruins — bottom-up containment machine built around the fissure.
  • Red Lady — wreck containing the Pearl and Fleet Intelligence Room.
  • Vel Orn — original theft site; shrine now without its anchor artifact.

Timeline

  • Pre-campaign: Fisk’s fleet steals the Pearl from Umberlee’s shrine at Vel Orn.
  • Fleet sinking: Umberlee sinks the fleet expecting recovery, then discovers the Pearl has fallen beyond her reach.
  • Vestra sinking: Leviathan destroys the Vestra; Auralis finds Perrin afterward.
  • 2026-05-16 world tick: Ridgeback follows the signal through; High Eyrie instruments register an anomaly.
  • 2026-05-16 world tick: Leviathan ranges into lower Shelfworks; heat event at 80 ft closes lower-tier salvage in practice.

Triggers

  • Party reaches the Shelfworks or Red Lady wreck.
  • Fisk accepts, refuses, or stalls Umberlee’s retrieval demand.
  • Perrin asks Auralis direct questions.
  • The party learns the Pearl is causing directed incursions.
  • Another fissure event fires during a world tick.

Blocks

  • Boundary-zone depth: instruments fail and conditions degrade.
  • Leviathan patrols within retrieval range.
  • Auralis does not volunteer the whole truth.
  • Umberlee and the party may want incompatible outcomes once the Pearl is recovered.

Consequences

  • Pearl recovered and removed: directed incursions stop; fissure remains a passive geological hazard.
  • Pearl returned to Umberlee: crisis quiets, but Umberlee regains a major soul artifact.
  • Pearl kept from Umberlee: party gains leverage and danger; Umberlee escalates.
  • Pearl left in place: more entities follow the signal; lower Shelfworks and Red Lady access deteriorate.
  • Auralis line fails: upper tiers flood, the gold rush collapses, and the Antheri machine is tested openly.

DM Notes

Auralis and the Antheri Machine

Auralis is a manufactured demigod — the last Antheri consciousness fused into an immortal framework engineered to survive the trench bottom. The visible Shelfworks are the newest layer of a bottom-up machine: vents, pressure bleeds, and safety architecture. Salvagers are pulling valves off a pressurized planar system.

Checks at the Shelfworks:

  • Perception DC 12: temperature drops and light changes colour below 80 ft.
  • Arcana/History DC 14: lower channels are too regular for habitation and too large for plumbing.
  • Investigation DC 15: salvage damage concentrates on flow/pressure-regulation structures.
  • Nature DC 13 + Sentinel records: identify safer approach windows to the Red Lady.

Party level 4–5 should work around or time the danger, not fight the Leviathan.

Umberlee Pressure

Branca stays polite until Fisk stalls too long. The Dead Lady exists to remind him what is at stake, not to kill him. Umberlee needs Fisk functional — killing him risks losing the five captains and the Pearl permanently.

Waveservants will not discuss the theological problem: Umberlee does not own the deepest water in the known world.

The Five Captains

Maren, Rael Corven, and three others are pressed into Delmar. Each has a thread that can surface via the mortis mechanic:

  • Maren — knows Halythion exists; personal lead from a sea elf friend.
  • Rael Corven — his Cloak of Useful Things went down with the Red Lady; potentially recoverable.

Open Questions

  • What third option exists besides returning the Pearl or leaving it?
  • Who commissioned the theft, and did they intend the Pearl to sink beyond Umberlee’s reach?
  • What exactly did the Antheri build the containment machine to prevent?
  • Why has the Leviathan not claimed the Pearl?
